evidence.why: Exact read/write sets and assertions.

reason: User configuration arrays are read, not mutated; only runtime fields and storage are changed. Assertions do not establish build-independent failure handling.

evidence.why: Shutdown restores interrupts before settings disables them again; allocations precede assertions.

reason: No rollback or checked failure return exists; assertions alone cannot exclude partial allocation state. Teardown and replacement are separately interrupt-bracketed, not one atomic lifecycle.

evidence.why: Processing recurrence, cursor updates and gain derivation.

reason: Canonical callback and settings confirm independent 160-sample feedback delay lines, Q7 gains, wet output replacement and per-channel modulo cursors; existing descriptions fit unchanged rendered names.

evidence.why: Settings lifecycle and initializer without explicit return.
Callback removal, old-effect shutdown, delay initialization and conditional registration.
External interrupt enable save/restore semantics.

reason: Initializer clears pointers then delegates to settings; driver copies configuration and registers context only on result 1. Existing explicit missing-return caveat is essential; success reporting refers to settings, not guaranteed C return propagation.
